page.layout: One column of running text on the page. Marginal notes stand in the left margin, beside the lines "Ob. 8." and "Episcop. idem habet." Printed page number 62 at the top left, running head at the top right. No catchword, signature or footnotes.

main_text.p: plenâ[?] per Dei gratiam fidei conditione, adeo-que impleto fœdere gratiæ, ex promissione euangelicâ, nos justi declaramur, & ex pacto euangelico cessant effectus iræ divinæ, hinc fide, ex hprafi scripturæ, recipimus λαμ-βάνομεν promissiones Dei Gal. 3. Itaqua[?] justificatio pactionalis non est nuda Dei acce-tantis nos, æstimatio, quasi nihil poneret in nobis: quamvis enim non ponat in nobis expulsionem habitus, & habitualis gratiæ novam introductionem, ut somniant pontificii attamen ponit aliquid reale in nobis nempe nos nostram propriam justitiam deseruisse, & justitiæ Christi propter remissionem peccatorum, firmiter adhærere coram judice, & aliud (esse) reale ponit in nobis nempe Dei actum justificandi terminatum in conscientiam nostram, quo non aliter quam debitor qui soluto, par fide-ijussorem, ære in quo erat, ita à foro recedimus nacti certificationem solutorum debitorum, quasi syngrapham à Christo absolutoriam.

Remmst. apol. f 113.Ob. 8. justitiam Christi nobis imputari propter meritum & obedientiam Christi, in rigore, non est verum, nisi dicamus justitiam Christi nobis impu-tari propter justitiam Christi, quod absurdum: & Episcop. idem habet.Episcop. disp. 22. de justif. thes. 5. Non est itaque justitia nostra justitia proprie Christi, nedum activa aut passiva sed id quod Christus utraque illa promeruit, & nos per solum Christum Iefum censequimur. page.notes: Doubtful readings: "plenâ" (first word, the line begins "pleta" with a tilde-like mark, possibly "plenâ"); "Itaqua" (could be "Itaque"); "hprafi" (unclear, possibly a corrupted or Hebrew-related word, copied as seen); "Remmst." (may be "Remonst."). Hyphenated line breaks kept: "adeo-que", "acce-tantis", "impu-tari", "fide-ijussorem", "cre-". The Greek "λαμ-βάνομεν" is hyphenated across the line. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The marginal note "Episcop. disp. 22. de justif. thes. 5." is placed where its mark stands in the text, and its exact punctuation in the scan is slightly uncertain. The word "justif." in that note is read from "ju-stif". The printed margin note is shown as "thef." in the scan and is rendered here as "thes.", which is a likely reading.
